about: 2-fer rule changes and the parks each one touches (Brandon Nov 9 2026, 4:37-4:42 PM CST: 'only redo the parts that changed'; KISS). A saved pair result is reused unless one of its two parks changed (outline, record ids, POTA pin / name, line) or a change below covers one of the parks. Add one entry per rule change: id (never reuse an id), when, why, and scope = {states: ['US-KY', 'CA-ON', ...], kinds: [words in the POTA park type, e.g. 'Wild and Scenic River'], flags: ['bad-pin', 'line']} or 'all' (every pair: emergency only). Emergency switch without an entry: KPC_FERS_FULL=1. The areas workflow also does ONE full area per run, round-robin (.github/fers-areas.json full_cycle_days). Nov 9 evening (KZ4CP 5:41 PM CST): a scope may also list park refs, 'parks': ['US-1234', ...]: only those parks are re-matched (their states are read again, every other park there keeps its result; for 2-fers every pair with a named park is tested again, so the parks touching it are rechecked too). A scope that lists nothing means ALL; a change that touches no park says scope 'none'.

changes.why: a park with a bad POTA pin (pin00 / 0,0) is tested by its saved record ids, never around its pin (run 42649544758)

When both parks already have an official agency outline, that layer is government or public land, so a blank owner field is not a hold. A blank owner whose outline is not from an official agency layer and is not an approximate or point-circle outline still cannot be a candidate.

Approximate outlines (picture traces and point-circles) do not block a 2-fer. The pair is an approximate 2-fer, drawn thinner and in a different color, with a note that it is not the official boundary and needs more research. WDPA / Protected Planet outlines are never a public 2-fer source.
A picture-trace outline never replaces an official outline already on file. Two parks that join the exact same official records go to the person-review list, not the candidate list.

Review fixes. Every pass reads a blocked-host layer from the key's saved copy; a missing saved copy holds the pair with a reason, and Wild and Scenic corridors come from saved records or the pair is held. Two parks on the same official records are an approximate 2-fer only when both POTA pins are inside the shared outline; otherwise the pair is held as a likely join to fix (pins and records listed on the row). Record ids are compared with their area and source; an outline with no source label is not official; a failed read never leaves a partial outline. A state feeds 2-fers only when its own index row was built on the current key rules.

A trail or river stretch counts only when at least 25 metres of the line run inside the other park (was no minimum). Pieces of one line that touch are measured together, to the line's real end. A line whose whole saved copy is under 25 metres is a broken copy: its pairs are held as not sure, never dropped. In a trail or river row the park that is not the line is graded by the current key like an area half (a key pin drops the row). A row's own stretch length is kept apart, so copies of other rows no longer shrink it.

No 2-fer rule changes and no pair is tested again: a pair's answer and its fingerprint are the same. What changes is which parks an area loads, when a pass stops and what it prints. An area is one box per group of states (a state more than 5 degrees from the others gets its own box) and a longitude east of 180 counts as past it, so Pacific loads Alaska, Hawaii and the West Coast plus their border neighbours, not all of North America (an area of touching states keeps exactly its old box). The pass prints a progress line every 200 pairs or 60 seconds, a line at the start of each stage and a heartbeat in a long stretch; the pair's fingerprint is inside its time limit; a pair cut by the pass's own time is left for the next run; the near-pairs list stops 4 minutes before the step's hard end so the pass still saves, and one near pair or n-fer test is cut when that time ends; the memory collect runs at most once a minute. KPC owner, 2026-11-12 (Quality on #154): a spot whose parks with their own outline are all filed under the area's states is the area's row even when its center is outside the pin boxes (Tongass National Forest x Misty Fjords National Monument, US-4448+US-4538, east of Misty Fjords' pin); a spot with a park of another area, or a line-only spot, still needs its center in the boxes. An n-fer stage cut for time marks the pass stopped for time: pass 1 keeps those areas' previous files (a new area is saved marked incomplete) and pass 2 / 3 leave the n-fer row waiting, never dropped.

A picture trace (data/fers-approx-outlines.json) can be an approximate 2-fer only when it sits inside a bigger park's outline: no part of the trace more than 25 yards (SHRINK) outside the other park's own area outline (official or the key's approximate outline), and that outline reaching more than 25 yards past the trace somewhere. Otherwise the row is dropped with the reason; two traces alone never make one. KPC owner, Nov 11 2026: official pins, trails and rivers COUNT under the existing rules, so a row with a point-circle park (the 100 ft circle; the card notes no boundary for that pin), a trail or a river is never touched by this rule and is decided exactly as before. The pair stays an approximate 2-fer with the not-official note, as before. Only pairs with one of these parks are tested again.

Rule R5 measured in full: a trail or water trail counts with another park within the full 100 ft (30.48 m) of the trail's centre line, or of the river's bank (no 5 m margin taken off; was 25.48 m). The station spot must still be 5 m inside the other park (STATION_IN, unchanged). Every pair with a line park is tested again.

The outline store switch-over. With KPC_FERS_FROM_STORE off (every ordinary run) no 2-fer answer and no pair fingerprint changes, so no pair is tested again (scope none, like 2026-11-11-area-boxes-time). With it on, a US or Canadian run reads park outlines, line parks' lines and water tiles from the outline store for the areas .github/fers-store-areas.json allows (all US and Canadian areas, an except list, US-KY never); an area the store does not hold is left out of the run with its reason. A store run stamps the parks of the areas it runs from the store with this id (kpc_fers_store.install wraps rule_stamp), so exactly those pairs are tested again, once, on their first store run. A live candidate row that a store run would turn NOT SURE only because the PAD-US closed areas or the ownership map could not be checked keeps its old row when it is the same spot (same place, size within 25 percent), tagged 'kept: not checked in a store run'. World areas are in the code behind their own switch, off ("world": "off"): no world pair is touched.

Fixes after the first 2-fer trial on the real outline store. (1) Passes 2 and 3 (every run, store or not): each row of the pass before takes at most one new spot of its pair and each spot goes to at most one row, best fit first (the spot's centre in the row's box, then the row's centre in the spot's box, then the largest share of the two boxes); a spot no row took, of a pair whose row was dropped in that pass, becomes a new row in pass 2 (pass 3 decides it) and in pass 3 (decided there); only a spot that cannot be added is a warning. Main gave the first touching spot to a row even when another row had taken it, so a real spot could be lost. No pair's spots change (the pair test is the same), only which row takes which spot, and that is worked out fresh in every run: no pair needs a new test. (2) Store runs only: a park held for licence is a known reason in pass 1 (no 'agency map did not answer' stop, no record ids printed); on a public store run a withheld park's rows of the previous public file are carried unchanged, marked 'not re-checked (outline held privately)', and counted per area (owner rule: never worse); the store words in the report; far line parks not listed; the run's total of withheld parks.

Owner rule 12 (2026-11-15, his words: "if we dont have state then pad it is"; "Yes to cpad or any other pad ...we use what we got and better 1 wins out"). Store core 3.6.3 gives a park whose records are not all publishable because some come from held layers a public view (publish_view 'public-records-only'): only the park's own publishable records, chosen by the engine's own precedence, covering at least 0.80 of the park. On a PUBLIC store run kpc_fers_store.py now reads such a park from its view records only (both the park and its index entry must name the same valid view; every view record is still judged publishable / basis / WDPA like any record) and never reads the held records; with no valid view the park needs the private store, as before. A private run and every non-store run are unchanged. Parks that were withheld become readable: their pairs are new (their outlines were never read on a public run), so they are tested anyway; no other pair changes.

Owner decision 2026-11-15 23:08 (his words: "lets go b for now and mark partial till we figure it out"; "little 2fer better then none and mark it partial boundary") and 23:14 ("We marking nothing not a 2 fer fyi... we just show what we think are overlaps .. offer partial boundaries when thats all we have"). (1) PARTIAL BOUNDARIES: store core 3.6.4 gives a held park whose own publishable records cover LESS than 0.80 of it a PARTIAL public view (publish_view 'public-records-partial', ratio at least 0.05, under its own view name so a reader that knows only the full view fails closed). A public store run USES it exactly like a full view (the held records are never read), marks every row that used it (partial_boundary with a plain why line), and never lets it take a 2-fer away: a partial piece lies INSIDE the park, so an overlap found with it is real and may be ADDED, while "no overlap" from it means UNKNOWN. A not-live row of such a pair is never written as a verdict: the previous public file's live row comes back unchanged (never worse) or no row is written at all, and carry_rows keeps the old status for such a pair instead of 'dropped: not found again'. (2) NOTHING IS EVER MARKED 'NOT A 2-FER': every 2-fer file, store run or not, public or Kentucky, now goes through kpc_fers.no_denials() at the write step. A row whose status denies a pair ('dropped: ...', 'dropped in pass N') is not written; when the file it replaces had a live row for that pair and kind, that row comes back unchanged (never worse); the reason goes to the run report's 'not shown' list for a person, never into a 2-fer file. The two row-bookkeeping statuses ('dropped: the same stretch twice (copy of ...)', 'merged into one row: ...') stay, and a row carried or kept from an older file is left exactly as it was (never worse, and the KPC-Store push check needs the exact copy). (3) WORLD AREAS OFF GITHUB: .github/fers-store-areas.json stays "world": "off", so every GitHub run is exactly as today; a run on a person's own machine may add the world areas with KPC_FERS_WORLD_STORE=on (ignored under GitHub Actions). It only adds areas: a world store run is still refused unless it is a PRIVATE store run, because world 2-fers are club room only. (4) PRIVACY GRADE 2026-11-16: a row that only carries a 'carried' stamp is no longer exempt from the no-denial rule (kpc_fers_store.carry_rows invents "dropped: not found again ..." for a pair with no partial-boundary park, which is a verdict of this run, so it is taken out and the last file's live row comes back unchanged); the per-pair reasons go to a private folder outside every git work tree (KPC_FERS_NOT_SHOWN_DIR / KPC_FERS_PRIVATE_OUT / KPC_FERS_PRIVATE_LOG) and the public run report keeps the COUNT only; the 2-fer reader pins the view basis to the owner's rule instead of only comparing the two sides; and a view ratio that is not a real number (a numeric string, True / False, None, NaN) fails closed. (5) RE-GRADE 2026-11-16: the stale 'not shown' list is stripped from the run report on EVERY run, not only one that suppressed something (the report is loaded from the file on disk); and the missing check's DROPPED list - a pair we looked at and did not show, with its reason - is kept out of the pushed data/fers/expected-<tag>.json and written to the private folder instead, the pushed file keeping the count, the pass flag, FOUND and NEVER LOOKED AT. No pair is re-tested by this change: a pair that had no row still has none, and a pair that had one keeps it.

KPC owner, 2026-11-16: world 2-fers opened. (1) .github/fers-ready-areas.json gets a W-* entry: since the Nov 8 gate was written, the Nov 9 rule takes the owner from a park's own record or agency name, the Nov 10 rule counts two official agency outlines as government or public land, and the POTA sub-park rule removed the same-agency block. (2) kpc_fers.ownership_step: the world branch used to return before the Nov 9 / Nov 10 tests, so a world pair inside two official agency outlines was 'not sure'; the world now takes the same tests first, then its own one-owner rule and 'no land register read for this country yet' wording. A pair with no owner on its records is still shown as 'not sure', never dropped. (3) kpc_fers_store: a world store run now reads the world parks from the store (its own saved_world, as saved_ca), and a world park's records are looked up the way the world store files them (<area>:<layer>:<id>); before this a test run of Belgium read 0 of its parks. US and Canadian parks are looked up by their ids as before. World 2-fers stay club room only (private store runs). key-rules-version.json fers stays v1 (the code change moves the hash by itself).
changes.scope_note: No US or Canadian pair changes: the code changes run only for world parks (REGION world). The world areas were never measured before, so they have nothing to re-test; they are new.

changes.why: Proof of work, round 1 (handoff of Nov 16, item 1 only). No 2-fer rule changes: which pairs count, their grades, rows and wording are the same. kpc_fers.py: every pass writes a receipt (counts only: parks expected, read, held with reason counts, pairs tested, rules hash, store date, engine version, seconds per stage, a verdict per area); the bot exits 84 when it stops before measuring and 85 when pass 1 read no outline of an area that has official parks (that area keeps its previous file and is never reported as having no 2-fers); an area the store does not hold is 'store missing' and a border area's missing store is counted as 'neighbour store missing: N parks'. kpc_fers_receipt.py check decides done from the receipt (not a rule file).
changes.scope_note: No pair answer or pair fingerprint changes: nothing is re-tested.

changes.why: Store runs do three passes of work, not four (KPC owner, 2026-11-16). The outline store gives every pass the same outline (about 2 m), so pass 2 (10 m grid, once fed by a fresher agency download) only repeated pass 3's test on a coarser grid. In a store run PASS=2 does nothing (exit 0, a receipt section that says so, no area file changed) and pass 3 takes every pass-1 row on the 5 m grid; a row pass 3 agrees with is marked for pass 2 too and the file keeps its pass2 date. A run that downloads from the agencies (no store) is unchanged. The pass loops of the workflows, the PC runner and the receipt check are unchanged (1, 2, 3, 5).
changes.scope_note: Measured on the same store and key, four passes against three: W-BE 6 = 6 candidates, W-NO 16 = 16, W-AT 53 = 53, W-CH 11 = 11, US-RI 6 = 6 (not sure 3 = 3), US-NY 66 = 66 (not sure 25 = 25); no shown pair lost or gained; US-NY gains 2 trail rows merged into rows already shown. Store areas are re-measured by their next run anyway; no area that does not use the store changes.

changes.why: A run named for some areas writes only those areas' files (KPC owner, 2026-11-16). Pass 1 also holds the neighbours' parks for border pairs and rewrote each neighbour's file as a pass-1 file; passes 2 to 5 take only the run's own areas, so the neighbour's finished rows were reset and never finished again. Measured: W-AT had 57 candidates, 39 merged rows and its pass 2/3/5 dates; after a W-CH run it had 53, 0 and none. With the change W-AT.json is byte for byte the same after the W-CH run. A whole-region run (no STATES) writes every area as before. No rule about what counts changes.
changes.scope_note: No pair answer changes: an area's own run gives the same rows as before. What changes is that another area's run no longer overwrites them.

changes.why: The public shelf of the outline store (KPC owner, 2026-11-16; Fable's brief). tools/kpc_store_public.py copies out of the private store only the parks whose every needed record passes the display copy's licence gate, in the same store format, and never lists the parks it leaves off. The reader (kpc_fers_store.py) learns one thing: when an area's index says shelf: public, a park the shelf does not have is held privately ('needs the private store', PRIVATE_WHY), exactly as a held park is when the full store is read. Without it such a park would be filed as missing from the store and NAMED on the store-filler list in a public file. Measured on the real US-RI store: 21 parks read identically from shelf and full store, 35 left off and every one held privately, none named. Fable's review of the change found three more ways a park left off a shelf could be named or measured wrongly, all fixed here: (1) a park with land in two areas, held in one: a record the key joins that the shelf does not have is held, not missing; (2) a trail or river park off the shelf (store_lines, its own path) is held, not listed as missing; (3) an area whose shelf holds no park still counts as a shelf. The export keeps each record's source (the reader skips a river line found on NHD by name) as one plain word only, and no longer copies publish_basis_detail.
changes.scope_note: No pair answer changes. The private store path is unchanged (test_a_reader_on_the_private_store_is_unchanged): a park the full store lacks is still 'not in the outline store'. The new branch acts only when a shelf is read.

changes.why: One program per area and one record lookup (handoff of Nov 16, items 2 and 4, on top of round 1, the store three-pass change, the own-areas-only change and the public shelf on main). No 2-fer rule changes: which pairs count, their grades, rows and wording are the same with the new switch off (the default). (1) kpc_fers.py + kpc_fers_store.py: a store run may run passes 1, 2, 3 and 5 in ONE process (kpc_fers_store.py chain), the store loaded once; each pass starts from the state a fresh process has, so the files are the same as four separate runs. Pass 2 of a store run still does nothing (main's three-pass rule, kept), and pass 3 still takes every pass-1 row. The spots the 5 m grid of pass 3 finds that no row took are listed privately on store runs; the switch KPC_FERS_FINE_ONLY (default off = today) would count them, and is the owner's decision. (2) kpc_record_key.py (new 2-fer rule file): the one function that turns a key join into a store record key for US, Canada and world; kpc_fers_store.store_ids calls it (same keys as #216).
changes.scope_note: No pair answer or pair fingerprint changes with the new switch off (the default): nothing is re-tested.

changes.why: A PUBLIC SHELF area too thin to be worth reading is left on the OLD path for that run, worked out from the shelf's own coverage block (tools/kpc_store_public.py writes parks_in_store / parks_on_shelf / share), not from a list kept by hand. Why it matters: in a thin area most parks are held, so a store run would CARRY most of its rows unchecked instead of re-testing them, which is worse than not using the store there at all. Measured 17 Nov from every store index: 85.2% of parks pass the licence gate overall, and 23 of 66 areas are under 90% (US-HI 9.5% to US-AK 89.2%). The floor is THIN_SHELF = 0.90, and KPC_FERS_SHELF_MIN overrides it (0 or 'off' = read every shelf area however thin). An area joins in BY ITSELF once enough of its layers have their terms confirmed on the PC store tool, so nothing is edited and no hash moves as coverage improves.
changes.scope_note: No pair answer changes. A thin area is handled exactly as one on the except list already was (verdict NOT USED, it keeps its previous files), the public 2-fer bot does not read the store at all yet, and the private store is never judged thin (only an index that says shelf: public carries a coverage block).

changes.why: D10 (owner ruling, 17 Nov 2026): a park on tripwire T1 (one of its records is joined to another park too), T2 (a piece of its land is cut off from its pin) or T4 (its pin is off its land and no person is behind the join) is NOT SURE for 2-fers until a person clears it; its outline stays on the map. kpc_fers.hold_tripwire() (passes 3 and 5, beside the no-ownership hold) turns every row of this run's verdict that shows a pair with a listed park into 'not sure: tripwire <ref> <T1+T4> (a person clears it; its outline stays on the map)'. The list is KPC-Data data/waiting/tripwires/not-sure.json, written by the tripwire bot (KPC-Data kpc_tripwires.py; a person's clears in data/waiting/tripwires/cleared.json are left out of it); the 2-fer workflows read it from their kpcdata/ checkout.
changes.scope_note: No pair answer changes and nothing re-runs: there is no list on KPC-Data yet and no 2-fer run is going (owner, 17 Nov: ground level first), and with no list hold_tripwire() holds nothing and adds no count line. Once the tripwire bot publishes a list, the next ordinary run of an area holds that area's listed parks' rows; no area is rebuilt for it.
